description.summary: protocol to assign icons to toplevels

protocol.description:
This protocol allows clients to set icons for their toplevel surfaces either via the XDG icon stock (using an icon name), or from pixel data.
A toplevel icon represents the individual toplevel (unlike the application or launcher icon, which represents the application as a whole), and may be shown in window switchers, window overviews and taskbars that list individual windows.
This file was transcribed by gowaku from the staging protocol of wayland-protocols, with shortened descriptions; the requests, events and their order are those of version 1.

interface.name: xdg_toplevel_icon_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface allows clients to create toplevel window icons and set them on toplevel windows to be displayed to the user.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the toplevel icon manager. This does not destroy objects created with the manager.

request.name: create_icon
request.description: Creates a new icon object. This icon can then be attached to a xdg_toplevel via the 'set_icon' request.

request.name: set_icon

description.summary: set an icon on a toplevel window

request.description: This request assigns the icon 'icon' to 'toplevel', or clears the toplevel icon if 'icon' was null. This state is double-buffered and is applied on the next wl_surface.commit of the toplevel. After this request, the icon is immutable, and the client may destroy it.

event.name: icon_size

description.summary: describes a supported & preferred icon size

event.description: This event indicates an icon size the compositor prefers to be available if the client has scalable icons and can render to any size, in surface-local coordinates.

arg.name: size
arg.summary: the edge size of the square icon in surface-local coordinates, e.g. 64

event.name: done
event.description: This event is sent after all 'icon_size' events have been sent.

interface.name: xdg_toplevel_icon_v1
interface.description: This interface defines a toplevel icon. An icon can have a name, and multiple buffers. In order to be applied, the icon must have either a name, or at least one buffer assigned.

entry.name: invalid_buffer
entry.summary: the provided buffer does not satisfy requirements

entry.name: immutable
entry.summary: the icon has already been assigned to a toplevel and must not be changed

entry.name: no_buffer
entry.summary: the provided buffer has been destroyed before the toplevel icon

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the icon object. A toplevel keeps an icon assigned to it.

request.name: set_name
request.description: This request assigns an icon name to this icon, which the compositor looks up in the icon theme.

request.name: add_buffer

description.summary: add icon data from a pixel buffer

request.description: This request adds pixel data supplied as wl_buffer to the icon. The buffer must be backed by wl_shm and must be square. Its contents must not change, and it must not be destroyed before the icon.

arg.name: scale
arg.summary: the scaling factor of the icon, e.g. 1
